record.paper_title: Problems and Conjectures Presented at the Third International Conference on Permutation Patterns (University of Florida, March 7-11, 2005)
record.original_question: For a permutation pi on [n], let P_pi be the poset on the values 1, ..., n ordered by i ≼ j when i ≤ j as integers and i occurs before j in pi; let conv(P) be the poset on the same elements in which i ≼_conv j exactly when the rank of i in P is at most the rank of j; and let conv(pi) be the unique layered permutation whose associated poset is isomorphic to conv(P_pi). Is it true that s_n(pi) ≤ s_n(conv(pi)) for every permutation pi and every natural number n?

evidence.quote: Given a poset P with rank function r, we let conv(P) denote the convex hull of P. The poset conv(P) is defined on the same set of elements as P, but in conv(P), i ≼conv j if and only if r(i) ≤ r(j) (in P).
For any permutation π there is a unique layered permutation, which we refer to as conv(π), such that Pπ ∼= Pconv(π).
Conjecture (Miklós Bóna): For any permutation π and natural number n, sn(π) ≤ sn(conv(π)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer n, let S_n denote the set of permutations of [n] = {1, 2, …, n}. Given a permutation π in S_n (written in one-line notation), define a poset P_π on the ground set {1, 2, …, n} by declaring i ≼ j (for i, j ∈ [n]) if and only if i ≤ j as integers and i appears weakly before j in the one-line notation of π. For any finite ranked poset (P, ≼) with rank function r, let conv(P) denote the poset on the same ground set as P defined by i ≼_conv j iff r(i) ≤ r(j) in P. A permutation σ ∈ S_n is called layered if it can be written as a concatenation of decreasing contiguous blocks whose entry values form consecutive increasing intervals (equivalently, σ avoids both 231 and 312). For every permutation π there is a unique layered permutation, denoted conv(π), such that P_{conv(π)} is isomorphic to conv(P_π).

For a permutation τ and integer n ≥ 1, let s_n(τ) denote the number of permutations in S_n that avoid τ as a (classical) pattern, i.e., that contain no subsequence whose relative order matches τ.

Prove or disprove: for every permutation π and every positive integer n,
   s_n(π) ≤ s_n(conv(π)).
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of Bóna's convex-hull conjecture comparing pattern-avoidance counts s_n(π) and s_n(conv(π)). The conjecture is listed among open problems from the 2005 Permutation Patterns conference, and no later paper located confirms a proof or disproof, so the current status is unknown to this search.
